In this sermon, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a close look at one of the most confronting moments in the entire Bible, where a man comes face to face with something so overwhelming it brings him to his knees. What follows is a sequence that is raw, unexpected, and oddly familiar. There is something in this passage that cuts through the noise of everyday life and asks a question most of us would rather not sit with too long. This is not a comfortable sermon, but it is an honest one, and it builds toward something worth hearing.

No pressure. Just press play when you're ready.

title: Eyes Wide Open
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Somewhere in Uganda, a man with almost nothing looked Ps Andrew Cartledge in the eye and smiled like someone who had everything. That small moment turned out to be the thread that unravelled something much bigger.

Ps Andrew Cartledge returns from Uganda with something he wasn't expecting, and it has nothing to do with what he saw on a screen or read in a book. In this episode, he shares an honest, unfiltered account of what it felt like to have his assumptions quietly dismantled, one encounter at a time. There are moments here that will make you rethink comfort, comparison, and what it actually means to rely on something bigger than yourself. This is not a guilt trip. It is an invitation to see differently.

Hit play and open your eyes.

title: Return To Your Shepherd
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb:
Have you ever felt like you've wandered so far off course that finding your way back seems impossible? Or maybe you're not even sure you've strayed at all, but something feels like it's missing?

In this episode, Ps Ruth Emmerson takes a look at one of the oldest images in human history and asks what it actually means for your life right now. She walks through what kind of shepherd Jesus really is, and the answer might surprise you, especially if you've always pictured God as someone waiting to correct you rather than come after you. This is a conversation about what it looks like to be truly known, truly led, and truly cared for, in every season, not just the easy ones.

Hit play and find out what kind of shepherd is actually looking for you.

title: Opportunity in the Ordinary
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
What if the moments that matter most aren't the big, dramatic ones, but the ones you almost walked right past? And what if you've already missed more of them than you'd like to admit?

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin takes a close look at a story from the book of Acts that is equal parts ordinary and extraordinary. He explores what it actually takes to notice what God might be doing in the middle of a busy, distracted, everyday life, and why being spiritually ready is only half the equation. There's something in here about a tuna pasta bake, a 3am prayer walk gone wrong, and a conversation that probably changed the course of someone's eternal life, all of which point to the same uncomfortable question: are we actually prepared to respond when the moment arrives?

Hit play and find out what Philip got right that most of us get wrong.

title: Communion - Bread and Blood
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the bread and wine of communion are pointing to something much older and much bigger than a church ritual? And what if the miracle of feeding thousands of people was never really about the food at all?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a familiar story and pulls back a layer most people never get to see. From a field in Galilee to a manger in Bethlehem to a cross outside Jerusalem, he traces a thread through scripture that connects bread, blood, and covenant in a way that makes the whole thing feel less like religion and more like a story that was always building toward something. If you have ever sat through a communion service and wondered what you were actually supposed to be feeling, this episode might help you understand why it matters more than you thought.

Hit play and follow the thread.

title: The Practice of the Presence
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
What if the hardest place you have ever been is actually exactly where you are supposed to be? And what if the key to surviving it, and maybe even thriving in it, has nothing to do with getting out?

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin shares a story from his own life that is equal parts honest and unexpected. He takes us into a world far from church culture, where his faith was treated less like something to be respected and more like a target. Along the way, he draws a surprising connection to one of the oldest figures in the Bible and what that ancient story might say about the situations we find ourselves in today. This is not a tidy, theoretical talk. It is personal, it is grounded, and it asks something real of the listener.

Hit play and find out what Ps Caleb discovered when he finally stopped talking to God about his circumstances and started listening.

title: Three Wise Women
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
Here are the show notes for this episode:

What do you do when life refuses to go according to plan? And what if the very thing standing between you and your future is actually preparing you for something far bigger than you imagined?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes a fresh look at three women from the Christmas story whose lives were marked by disappointment, uncertainty, and loss. Each one faced circumstances that could have broken them, and each one made a choice that changed everything. What they did in those moments, and why it mattered, might reframe the way you see your own waiting, your own grief, and your own unanswered prayers.

Press play and let these three wise women show you something you might have missed in the Christmas story.

title: How Then Shall We Live?
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the way you've always thought about living a good life has been missing something fundamental? And what if the gap between who you want to be and how you actually live isn't a willpower problem at all?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into a tension that most of us feel but rarely talk about honestly: the pull between the life we say we want and the habits we keep returning to. Drawing on the story of ancient Israel and some surprisingly raw reflections on his own struggles, Andrew walks through practices that are less about trying harder and more about reorienting everything. There is a moment in this sermon where he asks a question about holiness and what it means for how we represent Christ in ordinary life that might just stop you in your tracks. It is not a comfortable question, but it is a genuinely important one.

Hit play and let this one sit with you.

title: Kingdom-Centric Financial Habits
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the way you handle money says more about your faith than anything you'd ever say out loud? And what if the church has been too quiet about it for too long?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge tackles one of the topics people least expect to hear about on a Sunday morning, and does it without apology. He digs into some deeply held assumptions about wealth, generosity, and what it actually means to trust God with your finances. You might find yourself nodding along, or you might find yourself quietly uncomfortable, and either way that's probably a good sign.

If you've ever felt like financial freedom was for other people, or wondered whether faith and money even belong in the same conversation, this one is worth your time.

Hit play and find out what it looks like to hold your finances with an open hand.

title: Losing Control
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing standing between you and a deeper life with God isn't a lack of effort, but a grip you refuse to loosen? Most of us would say we trust God, but our daily choices tell a different story.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge gets honest about one of the most uncomfortable topics in the Christian life: submission. Not the kind that gets preached at you like a rule, but the kind that Jesus himself practised in the garden when everything in him wanted a different outcome. You'll hear a fresh take on the difference between commitment and submission, and why that distinction might be the thing that changes how you navigate authority, frustration, and the moments when life doesn't go the way you planned. This one will sit with you long after it ends.

Press play and see what happens when you start to loosen your grip.

title: How To Stay Close To God
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people already know what helps them stay close to God. The problem isn't knowledge. It's the gap between knowing and actually doing it.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge gets refreshingly honest about that gap, walking through some of the oldest, most tested spiritual practices in the Christian tradition and tackling head-on why so many people quietly give up on them. There's a moment in here where a simple email analogy reframes the whole conversation in a way that might just stick with you for days.

No pressure. Just press play when you're ready.

title: How To Come Close To God
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There is a gap between wanting to feel close to God and actually knowing how to get there. Most people assume it just happens, but what if that assumption is the very thing keeping them stuck?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church takes a hard look at why so many of us feel spiritually distant even when we genuinely want more. He draws on some surprising tensions in Scripture, a steak dinner analogy you will not forget, and a simple but confronting question about what we are actually offering God with our time. This is the first in a series exploring practices that have been around for centuries but that most modern believers have quietly abandoned without realising the cost.

If you have ever felt like God is far away and wondered whether that is just how it is, hit play.

title: The Good Portion
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you're working hardest to do for God is actually the thing pulling you furthest from him? And what if the answer isn't to do more, but to stop?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes a familiar story and asks an uncomfortable question about where we actually find ourselves in it. She unpacks the tension between doing and being, between serving and sitting, and why so many of us are spiritually running on empty despite giving everything we have. You might be surprised by what she says is the real cause of burnout, and even more surprised by what she says is the cure. This is not a guilt trip about what you are missing. It is more like a conversation about what is already waiting for you.

Press play and find out what it means to choose the good portion.

title: The Prayer of Faith
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**Can prayer actually do something, or is it just something we say when we don't know what else to do?** Most of us have been in a situation where we felt completely out of options, and the honest question underneath all of it is: does anyone actually hear this?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the most specific and practical passages in the Bible about prayer and healing, and what he finds there might challenge some assumptions you didn't even know you had. There's a kind of prayer described in James chapter 5 that is very different from the vague, hopeful kind most of us default to, and Andrew makes a sharp distinction between the two. He also gets into why forgiveness and unconfessed sin might be more connected to physical healing than most people ever consider, and what it actually looks like for a church community to take that seriously together.

Hit play and find out what the "prayer of faith" really means, and why it might matter more than you think.

title: Warnings Against Sin
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Honestly, most of us assume we're doing okay spiritually as long as we're not doing anything obviously wrong. That assumption might be worth questioning.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through a passage in James that has a way of getting under your skin. He unpacks three specific patterns that most people never think of as sin, and at least one of them will probably sound uncomfortably familiar. There's a story from a village in the Philippines that stops the sermon in its tracks, a reference to the final episode of Seinfeld that lands harder than you'd expect, and a question about your own community that might be harder to shake than you'd like.

If you're someone who tends to feel quietly confident about where your life is headed, this one is especially for you.

title: The War Within
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Have you ever felt like the biggest battle you're facing isn't out there in the world, but somewhere deep inside yourself? And what happens when that internal war starts spilling over into your relationships, your community, and even your church?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into one of the most honest and confronting passages in the New Testament, and what he finds there might make you uncomfortable in the best possible way. He tackles some questions most of us quietly wrestle with: why do we keep doing the things we hate, why do Christians fight each other, and why do we expect the world to behave like it already knows Jesus? There is a moment in this sermon where he makes a point about judgment and the world that is genuinely surprising, and it has a way of shifting how you see things around you. The answer he lands on is simple, but sitting with it is anything but easy.

Hit play and find out what it actually looks like to stop fighting the war on your own terms.

title: The Right Tools
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**What if the tools you need to face life's hardest moments are ones you already have access to, but just haven't picked up yet?**

Most of us walk into difficult situations feeling underprepared, whether that's conflict at home, pressure at work, or the quiet sense that something bigger is working against us. But what if the problem isn't your circumstances, it's that you haven't equipped yourself properly for them?

In this Father's Day sermon from Harvest Church, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a familiar passage from Ephesians and makes it feel anything but familiar. Expect tool belts, steel cap boots, a fire extinguisher, and one very stubborn belt buckle. Beneath the laughs, though, there's a genuinely honest conversation happening about strength, what it really means, where it actually comes from, and why so many people are walking through life without the things they need most.

Hit play and see what it looks like to actually be equipped for the life you're living.

title: The War of Wisdom
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the wisdom you've been relying on is actually working against you? And what if the line between genuine insight and something far more dangerous is thinner than you think?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge unpacks a tension hiding inside a few short verses from the book of James, and the picture it paints is surprisingly confronting. There are two kinds of wisdom on offer, and according to James, one of them is described in terms that might genuinely catch you off guard. This isn't a neat self-help framework. It's a honest look at what drives our decisions, our comparisons, and our ambitions, and what it actually looks like to operate from something better.

Hit play and find out which kind of wisdom has been shaping your life.

title: What do you Want
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Imagine sitting down with someone who asks you one question and then just waits. Not for the polished answer, not for what sounds good, but for what you actually want. For your life, your family, your community.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes that question somewhere you might not expect. Along the way you will hear about a one-of-a-kind pair of shoes, a stranger showing up at a front door, and a servant who climbs a mountain seven times looking for something that isn't there yet. This is a sermon about vision, about the gap between what we can see and what might actually be possible, and about why so many of us stay stuck somewhere in between.

If you have been sitting with a sense that something more is possible but you can't quite name it, this is probably the right episode for this moment.

title: Taming the Tongue
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
The tongue is the one part of you that can build someone up and tear them apart with equal ease, sometimes in the same conversation. That tension sits right at the heart of James chapter 3, and it turns out the Bible has more to say about it than most of us are comfortable admitting.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a close look at one of the most honest and uncomfortable passages in the Bible. He walks through the kind of tongue trouble most of us recognise but rarely talk about openly, from gossip and harsh words to outbursts of anger and the quiet poison of flattery. There are no easy answers here, but there is a surprisingly practical framework for understanding why our words get away from us, and what it actually looks like to bring them under control.

By the end, you will have a clearer picture of what James actually says about the one part of your body that might be running the rest of your life, and a few honest questions worth sitting with.

title: Childlike Faith
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
They say faith can move mountains, but nobody tells you that getting there might mean unlearning almost everything you thought you knew.

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin brings a refreshingly honest perspective to a passage that is easy to skip past but hard to sit with once you really hear it. He asks what it actually means to have a childlike faith, not in a sentimental way, but in a way that might quietly challenge where you've landed in your own journey. From a shopping bag full of bricks to a very embarrassing skate park incident, Caleb uses some genuinely funny moments to get at something that cuts a lot deeper. This one will make you laugh and then make you think.

Press play and find out what Jesus was really getting at when he told a group of grown adults to become like children.

title: Free Flowing Faith
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**What if the way you've been "doing church" is actually making things worse?**

Most of us assume that more input equals more growth. More sermons, more worship, more Bible reading. But what if there's a hidden problem that no one is talking about, and it might be the very reason so many people feel stuck, flat, or spiritually empty?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a detour through the Dead Sea, the book of James, and one of the most unexpectedly honest metaphors you'll ever hear in a church setting. He lays out six signs that something might be blocking your faith from actually going anywhere, and then gets into what it looks like when faith stops being something you collect and starts being something that moves. It's direct, it's a little uncomfortable, and it just might be the conversation you didn't know you needed.

Hit play and find out which side of the equation you're actually on.

title: Triumph over Temptation
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Everyone faces temptation. But why do some people seem to overcome it while others keep circling back to the same struggle, no matter how hard they try?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into something most of us would rather not admit: that the things we keep getting pulled toward say something real about what is already inside us. He unpacks why temptation rarely starts big, how the world keeps quietly shifting the goalposts on what is and is not acceptable, and what it actually looks like to stand firm when giving in seems like the easier, smarter, or even more reasonable choice. Through two very different biblical stories, he shows what triumph over temptation can cost you, and why it is still worth it.

Hit play and find out what is really fuelling the pull you feel toward the things you know you should walk away from.

title: Faith Under Fire
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Faith is supposed to hold you together when life falls apart. But for a lot of people, it's the first thing that goes.

In this opening episode of a brand new series through the Book of James, Ps Andrew Cartledge brings something deeply personal into the room, something raw and unresolved, and uses it to explore what it actually means to hold on when the ground disappears beneath you. This isn't a tidy sermon with easy answers. It's an honest look at why hard things happen to faithful people, and what James has to say about the kind of faith that survives the fire.

If you're someone who has believed, trusted, done everything right, and still watched something fall apart, this one is for you.

title: Tools of the Trade
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb:
**What if the tools you need for the hardest moments of your life have been sitting right in front of you the whole time?**

Most people think of church as the place where spiritual things happen, and home as somewhere else entirely. But what if that divide has been costing you more than you realise?

In this episode, Ps Ruth Emmerson brings a warmth and directness that makes you feel like you are sitting across from someone who genuinely wants you to win at life. She walks through a set of practical tools that are designed not just for Sunday mornings but for 10pm moments in your bedroom, for weeks when sickness won't lift, for when the accusing voices feel louder than anything else. This is not a lecture about trying harder. It is more like being handed something you did not know you were missing.

Hit play and find out what belongs in your toolbox.

title: Pentecost
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
One hundred and twenty people are sitting in a room in Jerusalem, waiting. Jesus told them to go, and then told them to stay. So they wait, for ten days, while the city fills up around them with thousands of pilgrims arriving for one of the most important festivals on the Jewish calendar.

Most people assume Pentecost got its name from the day the Holy Spirit showed up. But what if that assumption has been quietly flipping the whole story upside down? And what if the timing of that day wasn't a coincidence at all?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a familiar story and starts pulling on threads that most people walk right past. Why did Jesus tell his followers to go, but then immediately tell them to wait? Why that specific day, out of every day on the calendar? And what does an ancient Jewish harvest festival have to do with the birth of a movement that spread across the known world in a matter of months? There is a strategy buried in this story, and once you see it, the whole thing looks different.

You won't hear Pentecost the same way again.

title: Walk This Way
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**What does it actually cost to be made right with someone you've deeply wronged, and what happens when you can't pay that price yourself?**

Most of us carry some version of that question, even if we've never put it into words. This episode of the Harvest Church sermon series digs into a corner of the Bible that most people quietly skip over because the language feels too big and too ancient to matter today.

Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a single word from a letter written two thousand years ago to a church in crisis, a community pulled in every direction by competing voices and cultural pressure, and unpacks why that word might be the most important thing you hear this week. What he builds toward is unexpected, and the courtroom picture he paints near the end is worth staying for.

Hit play and find out what that word actually means, and why it changes everything about how you understand where you stand.

title: Holy Spirit Boldness
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
Most of us already know what we should do. We know the conversation we should have, the risk we should take, the moment we should step forward. And still, somehow, we don't. That gap between knowing and doing is uncomfortable to admit, but it's exactly where this episode begins.

Ps Rachel Cartledge from Harvest Church takes an honest look at why good intentions so rarely translate into actual action, and her answer isn't what you'd expect. She digs into the story of two ordinary fishermen who went from hiding in fear to standing boldly in front of the most powerful people in the room, and the question she asks about what changed for them is one worth sitting with. Along the way she gets refreshingly real about her own moments of hesitation and disappointment, and she reframes what boldness actually looks like in everyday life in ways that might surprise you.

This episode asks you to take a careful look at the distance between what you say you want and how you're actually living. That kind of honesty doesn't cost nothing.

title: Revival Ready
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if you've been chasing something your whole faith life without really knowing what it is? And what if that confusion is actually keeping you further from the thing you're desperate for?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes an honest and sometimes uncomfortable look at one of the most misunderstood words in Christian culture. He unpacks what revival actually is, what it definitely is not, and why so many people spend years running after a counterfeit version of the real thing. Along the way, he introduces five types of people who each have a very different relationship with revival, and chances are, you will recognise yourself in at least one of them.

If you have ever wondered whether there is something more, or whether what you have experienced is the genuine article, press play.

title: How to Build Your Life
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What are you actually building your life on? Not what you think you are, but what your daily choices reveal you are.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the most familiar stories in the Bible and finds something in it that most people completely miss. He asks a question that sounds simple on the surface but gets uncomfortable fast: when the storms come, and they will come, what is actually holding you up? This is not a gentle pat on the back. It is an honest look at priorities, values, and the gap between what we say matters to us and how we actually spend our time and energy.

Hit play and find out what it looks like to build a life that holds.

title: One Thing - Inquire
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you think is growing your faith is actually just one piece of a much bigger picture? And what if the piece you're missing is the one that makes everything else actually work?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge wraps up the "One Thing" series through Psalm 27 verse 4 with a look at what it really means to inquire, to study, to sit at the feet of Jesus. He brings two ideas together that you might not expect to find in the same sermon, and the tension between them is worth sitting with. There are some honest questions here about how we learn, where we learn, and whether we have quietly been leaning on the wrong things to carry weight they were never meant to carry. This one does not let you off the hook easily, but it does not leave you without somewhere to go.

Press play and find out which piece you might be missing.

title: One Thing - Gaze
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the way you see the world is actually shaping who you are becoming? And what if the thing you need most is not more information, but a completely different way of looking?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a single verse from the Psalms and unpacks something that is surprisingly easy to miss: there is a difference between what your eyes take in and what your heart actually sees. You will hear a story from Genesis that reframes everything you thought you knew about making good decisions, a question that is harder to answer than it first appears, and an honest look at why so many of us are gazing at the wrong things without even realising it. This is not about trying harder or being more spiritual. It is about something much simpler, and much more disorienting, than that.

Hit play and find out what it actually means to gaze.

title: One Thing - Dwell
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you're searching for most isn't somewhere you need to go, but somewhere you need to stay? And what if you've been running from the very place that was always meant to feel like home?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes one word and unpacks it in a way that might shift how you think about your everyday life. Drawing on some of the most recognisable stories and passages in the Bible, he explores what it actually looks like to stop striving, stop rushing, and simply remain. There's a question woven through this whole conversation that's worth sitting with: what does the fruit of your life say about where your roots are planted?

Press play and spend some time with this one.

title: One Thing - Seek
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you are searching for most, whether it is healing, belonging, peace, or something you can barely name, is actually pointing you toward something much bigger? And what if the way you pursue that thing matters just as much as finding it?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up about seeking, not in a vague spiritual sense, but in a way that is surprisingly honest and grounded. He talks about the difference between chasing outcomes and chasing the source of those outcomes, and why that distinction changes everything. He gets refreshingly candid about his own insecurities as a pastor, the moments where he has felt least qualified yet seen the most happen, and what that taught him about where real transformation actually comes from. Along the way, he draws on some ancient texts and some very modern questions to build a picture of what it actually looks like to pursue God with that kind of bold, persistent, slightly-unreasonable hunger.

Hit play and find out why "impudence" might be the most important word you hear this week.

title: One Thing - Ask
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the one thing you've been missing isn't a better routine, a fresh start, or even more effort? What if it's something far simpler, and far harder, than any of that?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes an ancient poem, a queen who risked her life to walk into a king's throne room, and a personal story of unanswered prayer and weaves them into something that might just reframe the way you think about asking for what you need. He doesn't tidy everything up or promise easy answers. What he does do is make a case that most of us aren't asking too much, we're asking too little of the right things. There's a moment in this episode where Andrew gets unexpectedly honest about his own faith being tested, and it's worth staying for.

Hit play and see where this one takes you.

title: One Thing
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing pulling you away from what matters most isn't actually a bad thing, just the wrong thing? And what if the answer isn't doing more, but actually doing less?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church digs into a question that feels almost countercultural right now: what does it look like to fix your attention on just one thing in a world that is constantly splitting it in a hundred directions? Drawing from a single verse in the Psalms, he traces a thread that runs through the lives of David, Mary and Martha, and the Apostle Paul, and makes a case that the ancient habits we've quietly abandoned might be exactly what we need most today. This isn't about getting your quiet time routine right. It goes deeper than that.

Hit play and find out what the one thing actually is.

title: Planted
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What if the secret to lasting happiness isn't found in anything you can buy, experience, or chase, but in something as simple as where you are planted? And what if the answer has been sitting in an ancient poem this whole time?

In this sermon, Ps Rachel Cartledge opens up Psalm 1 in a way that feels less like a Bible study and more like a conversation about the choices that quietly shape everything. She draws on the kind of imagery you can actually see and feel, roots, rivers, storms, and trees that don't move, to explore what it really means to be grounded when life gets hard. Whether you're in a dry season right now or just trying to figure out which direction to head, this one will make you think about the paths you're on and why they matter more than you might realise.

Press play and find out which way you're leaning.

title: Profitable Christianity Part Two
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the things holding your faith back aren't the big dramatic struggles, but the simple, everyday habits you've been quietly avoiding? And what if belonging to a church community actually asks something specific of you, not just your attendance, but something deeper?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge walks through what it genuinely looks like to be part of a church, not just to attend one. He lays out nine responsibilities that come with belonging, and while none of them are complicated, together they paint a picture that might quietly challenge the way you've been showing up, or not showing up, to your faith community. This is the kind of straight-talking, no-nonsense conversation about church that most people never actually have out loud.

Hit play and find out what it really costs to be part of something bigger than yourself.

title: Profitable Christianity Part One
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Honestly, most of us have never really sat down and counted the cost of belonging somewhere. We sign up, we show up, and we quietly hope the benefits outweigh whatever we have to give.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church digs into what he calls "profitable Christianity," and it is not what you might expect from that phrase. He walks through an idea that most people quietly resist: that being part of a community means accepting both the rewards and the weight that come with it. Using a surprisingly relatable comparison that moves from babies to bills, he builds a case that will make you rethink what you have been signing up for, or maybe avoiding altogether.

By the end, you will know exactly which side of the ledger you are on.

title: Practical Christianity
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
**What does it actually look like to live out your faith when life is already full and demanding?** Most of us have a gap between what we believe and how we actually spend our time, energy, and resources. That gap can feel uncomfortable, even a little convicting.

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes a close look at the earliest followers of Jesus and what set them apart, not their theology, not their Sunday attendance, but something far more practical and surprisingly personal. She unpacks three areas where real, everyday generosity shows up in a person's life, and the answer to one of them might catch you off guard. There is also a refreshingly honest take on busyness, and why saying no to some things might actually be the most generous thing you can do.

Hit play and find out what practical Christianity looks like when it gets off the page and into your week.

title: Purposeful Christianity
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the way you've been trying to balance everything in your life is actually the very thing making it harder? And what if the problem isn't that you're doing too little, but that you've been standing in the wrong spot?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church digs into what it actually looks like to live with purpose rather than just good intentions. He tackles a tension that most people feel but rarely name, the pull between the life you want and the life you're actually living. Along the way, he challenges some assumptions that even long-time churchgoers rarely stop to examine, and he doesn't let himself off the hook either. This one gets honest in ways that are uncomfortable and oddly freeing at the same time.

Hit play and find out where you've been standing.

title: Peripheral Christianity
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**What's Actually at the Center of Your Life?**

Most of us would say Jesus is at the center of our lives. But what if the way we actually live tells a different story?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through Ephesians chapter one and asks a question that sounds simple but lands harder the longer you sit with it: is your faith central, or has it quietly drifted to the edges? You will hear a fresh look at what it actually means to be "in Christ," not just in belief but in practice, including an honest conversation about why so many people genuinely love Jesus but keep the church at arm's length. It is the kind of sermon that starts warm and gets uncomfortable in the best possible way.

Hit play and find out where you are really standing.

title: The Church People or Place
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There's a version of church that most people have accepted without ever really questioning it. The building, the Sunday routine, the event you show up to and then leave. It feels normal because it's familiar, but Ps Andrew Cartledge thinks it might be costing us something we didn't even know we'd lost.

In this episode, Ps Andrew from Harvest Church works through some of the biggest questions people quietly carry about what church actually is, why it exists, and whether it even matters in the world we live in now. He challenges a comfortable assumption that most people, inside the church and out, have never really stopped to examine. What he lands on might reframe not just how you see church, but how you see yourself.

Is it possible you've been showing up to something and missing the whole point of it?

title: The In Between
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What do you do when you're stuck somewhere between where you started and where you're supposed to be? Not lost exactly, just not there yet, and with no clear sign of how much further you have to go.

Ps Rachel Cartledge brings a message that starts with a hiking trip through the Canadian Rockies and ends up somewhere much closer to home. She walks through one of the most familiar stories in the Bible, the Israelites wandering between Egypt and the Promised Land, and finds in it something surprisingly honest about what it feels like to be in a season that makes no sense. If you have ever felt like you are heading in the wrong direction, or standing completely still when everything in you wants to move, this episode is going to resonate.

Press play and find out what it actually means to trust the route when you cannot see where it leads.

title: Enter His Presence
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most of us have been showing up to church the wrong way our entire lives.

Ps Andrew Cartledge takes an honest and at times uncomfortably familiar look at the habits we bring into a church service without even realising it. He draws on an unexpected source, a book that challenges the way modern Christianity has quietly drifted into something it was never meant to be, and he walks through an ancient structure that might reframe everything you thought you knew about what it means to show up. This is not a gentle nudge. It is a genuine rethink of who church is actually for, and the answer might surprise you.

Worth the listen.

title: Closer
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Not more effort. Just closer.

The distance you feel from God might not be a mystery to solve. It might be a choice you're making without even realising it. In this sermon from Harvest Church, Ps Andrew Cartledge unpacks one of the most straightforward invitations in the Bible and asks why so many of us keep God at arm's length. Along the way he explores what actually happens to a person when they stop treating faith like a Sunday appointment and start treating it like a relationship worth showing up for every day. There are five things that begin to shift in your life when you move closer, and five habits that make that closeness possible. You might be surprised which ones you're already neglecting.

Maybe the question isn't whether there's more to faith than going through the motions. Maybe it's what you're going to do once you know there is.

title: The Power of Passed On Promises
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the most important thing you ever did wasn't something you finished yourself? What if the whole point was to hand it on?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a hard look at what it actually means to live a life that matters, not just in the moment, but across generations. He draws on one of the most famous chapters in the Bible and finds something in it that most people walk straight past. Along the way, he brings in a half-finished monument carved into a South Dakota mountain, a man named Noah who quietly checked out for three hundred years, and a personal story about his own father that gets right to the heart of what this whole thing is really about. This is not a comfortable conversation, but it is an honest one, and it raises a question you will keep thinking about long after you finish listening.

Hit play and find out what separates the people who were still living by faith when they died from the ones who just showed up regularly.

title: Your Words Are Your Weapons
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb:
**Your words might be doing more damage than you realize, and not always in the ways you expect. What if the thing holding you back is something you do dozens of times a day without even thinking?**

Ps Ruth Emmerson brings something refreshingly honest to this conversation about the words we speak, the words we receive, and the gap between what we mean to say and what actually lands. She gets personal, she gets practical, and she doesn't let anyone off the hook, including herself. This is the kind of sermon that starts with a tube of toothpaste and ends with you rethinking something you said before you even got out of bed this morning.

Press play and find out why your mouth might be the most underestimated weapon you own.

title: The Baptism of the Holy Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if everything you thought you knew about how God works was only part of the story? And what if the part you were missing changed everything about how you approach your own spiritual life?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a close look at three moments from the book of Acts where the same Spirit showed up in completely different ways, to completely different people, in a completely different order than anyone expected. He walks through the texts carefully, honestly, and with a lot of warmth, and somewhere in the middle of it all, a picture starts to emerge that quietly dismantles some of the assumptions many of us carry into church without even realising it. Whether you grew up in church or you are just starting to ask questions about what faith actually looks like in real life, there is something in this one that will get under your skin.

Hit play and find out why the moment Peter was still mid-sentence might be the most important detail in the whole story.

title: The Power of the Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing you've been straining to do on your own was never meant to be done that way? What if the power you need has been available the whole time, and you just haven't been connected to it?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes one verse from the book of Acts and unpacks something that a lot of people quietly wrestle with: the gap between the life they know they're supposed to be living and the life they're actually living. Using a story about a broken-down car and a missionary who spent two years doing things the hard way, Andrew explores what it really looks like when someone stops relying on their own devices and plugs into something bigger. The transformation of one of history's most unlikely speakers sits at the centre of this episode, and it raises a question you won't be able to shake easily.

Hit play and find out what changes when the connection is finally made.

title: Promise of the Holy Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the Holy Spirit isn't who you've been told he is? And what if the way most of us think about him has been quietly limiting everything we experience of God?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a long, honest look at who the Holy Spirit actually is, starting from the very first verses of Genesis and tracing a thread that runs all the way through to Jesus himself. Along the way, he challenges an idea that has settled into the language of church without much scrutiny, and the shift in perspective it opens up is not a small one. If you have ever felt like your experience of God was somehow dependent on you doing the right thing or saying the right words first, this one is going to sit with you.

Hit play and find out why Ps Andrew thinks the Holy Spirit catching our train, not the other way around, changes everything.

title: Jesus is Part Three
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the gap between you and God is bigger than any self-improvement, religion, or good intention could ever bridge? And what if someone already crossed it, not as a helper, but as the whole bridge itself?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge unpacks one of the most misunderstood roles of Jesus, exploring why he is described as a mediator and what that actually means for ordinary people. Drawing on ancient roles of prophets, priests, and kings, Andrew builds a picture of Jesus that is far bigger and more surprising than most people have considered. There is a moment in this sermon where a single word from a 2000 year old text reframes everything, and once you hear it framed this way, it is hard to unsee.

Hit play and find out why the bridge matters more than you might think.

title: Jesus is Part Two
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if everything you thought you knew about Jesus was only half the picture? And what if the part you're missing makes the whole thing harder, not easier?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into who Jesus actually was when he walked the earth, and some of what he finds might surprise you. This is not the gentle, agreeable figure you might have grown up hearing about. The sermon explores Jesus as a teacher whose message cut against the grain of his culture and raised the bar rather than lowering it, leaving his listeners with more to wrestle with, not less. Along the way there are honest questions about how we read ancient texts, what Jesus was really getting at when he asked "who do you say that I am," and why the impossibility of his teaching might actually be the whole point.

Hit play and find out what Jesus was actually saying.

title: Jesus is
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There is a version of Jesus that most of us have been carrying around for years, assembled quietly from the people who raised us, the experiences that shaped us, and the culture we swim in every day. It feels familiar. It might even feel certain. But at some point, if you are honest, you realise you have never really stopped to work out what you actually think.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church takes a question that Jesus himself asked his closest followers and turns it directly on the listener. It is a question that sounds simple on the surface but gets more uncomfortable the longer you sit with it. You will hear why building your faith on feelings and good experiences alone might be leaving you more exposed than you think, and why the answer Peter gives in Matthew 16 is far more loaded and historically significant than most people ever stop to consider.

If you have never really wrestled with who you say Jesus is, this might be a good moment to start.

title: Battle For the Bible
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Here are the show notes for this episode:

Have you ever stopped to wonder if the Bible is actually worth trusting, or if it is just an ancient book that no longer applies to real life? And what if the biggest threat to that book is not coming from outside the church, but from within it?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes on one of the most urgent questions facing Christians today: how do we hold onto a book that the world, and sometimes even the church, keeps telling us is outdated, irrelevant, or just plain wrong? You will hear where the attack on the Bible actually starts, why it matters more than most people realise, and what is genuinely at stake when we stop taking Scripture seriously. This is not a dry theology lecture. It is a straight-talking conversation about something that shapes everything.

Hit play and find out why the battle for the Bible might be the most important one you are not thinking about.

title: The Table
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What if the most ordinary thing you do every day, sitting down to eat, is actually one of the most spiritually significant things you can do? And what if the reason community feels so hard to find right now is because we have quietly stopped doing something we were always meant to do?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes a simple, familiar image, the table, and unpacks why it keeps showing up at the centre of some of the most important moments in history, and in our own lives. She traces a pattern hidden across three separate stories in the book of Luke that reveals something surprising about blessing, brokenness, and what it means to be given to others. Along the way she reflects honestly on family, memory, and the kind of connection that does not happen in a course or a program but around a meal with real people. This one will make you think differently about your kitchen, your calendar, and maybe even your backyard shed.

Pull up a chair and press play.

title: Present in the Presence
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if you've been showing up to the right place your whole life, but missing what's actually there? What if presence and being truly present are two completely different things?

In this sermon, Ps Andrew Cartledge explores what it really means to encounter God rather than just attend church. He works through some unexpected stories, some honest confessions, and some passages of Scripture that reframe what power, peace, and purpose actually look like when you stop going through the motions. There's a question in here that might catch you off guard, and once it lands, it's hard to shake.

Hit play and find out what you might be holding in your hands without even realising it.

title: Clothed in Love
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**What does it actually mean to love someone the way you're supposed to?**

Most of us have heard the word "submit" and either cringed or cheered, depending on which side of the relationship we're on. But what if the whole conversation has been starting from the wrong place?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the most misunderstood passages in the Bible, and the closer he looks, the more the familiar surface reading starts to shift. He digs into the original Greek, the cultural context, and what Paul was actually asking of each person in a household, and the answers might surprise you. This isn't a comfortable sermon that leaves everyone feeling validated. It's the kind of honest unpacking that asks something real of everyone in the room, husbands especially.

Hit play and find out what it looks like to stop wearing the wrong things and finally put on love.

title: Turning Misery into Mission
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
They say suffering produces perseverance, but nobody tells you what to do while you are still in the middle of it. Paul did not write his letter to the Colossians from a comfortable chair. He wrote it from a cell, and somehow that changes everything about how you read it.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into a part of that letter most of us quietly skip over because it makes us uncomfortable. There is something unexpectedly honest here about the gap between the version of faith we were sold and the one Paul actually lived. Andrew brings a raw, sometimes self-deprecating look at what it means to be on mission when life is genuinely hard, and he unpacks a word buried in the original Greek that quietly reframes everything about why you are here.

Sit with this one.

title: What Are You Wearing
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Imagine someone who genuinely cares about you, someone who knows you well, pulling you aside and asking a simple question: "What are you wearing?"

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes that surprisingly everyday question and turns it into something that cuts much deeper. Using a passage from the book of Colossians, he unpacks the idea that every person is wearing something spiritually, whether they know it or not. Some of it is fresh, some of it is worn out, and some of it has been sitting unopened in a closet for years. This is a conversation about identity, about what we carry into each day, and about why so many people keep reaching for the same tired clothes when there is a whole wardrobe waiting for them.

Hit play and find out what you might have been wearing without even realising it.

title: Believers Beware
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**Believers Beware**

What if some of the biggest threats to your faith don't come from outside the church, but from inside it? And what if they sound completely reasonable when you first hear them?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a close look at a two-thousand-year-old letter that reads like it was written for today. He unpacks two specific warnings buried in the book of Colossians, warnings about the kinds of ideas and religious pressure that can quietly pull people away from what actually matters. This is not a comfortable, everything-is-fine kind of message. It asks hard questions about what we believe, where those beliefs come from, and whether we are building on something solid or just going along with whatever sounds good.

Hit play and find out what Paul was so worked up about from inside a prison cell, and why it still matters now.

title: Jesus Over Everything
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What does it actually mean to say Jesus is "over everything"? Not as a bumper sticker slogan, but as something that reshapes the way you see the world, your choices, and what you put your trust in?

In this first episode of a four-week series through the book of Colossians, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into a letter written from a prison cell that somehow manages to feel like a warm embrace. The questions it raises are ones people are still wrestling with today: Is Jesus enough on his own, or do we quietly add things to him to feel more complete? What does it mean that he holds all things together? Andrew brings some surprising history, a Leonardo da Vinci story you might not have heard, and a very honest moment about patience that most people will relate to immediately.

Press play and find out why a letter written in chains almost two thousand years ago might be exactly what you need to hear right now.

title: Power & Authority
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if having power and having authority are not the same thing, and confusing the two is costing you more than you realise? And what if the thing you think you need most is actually secondary to something you have already been given?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge unpacks a distinction that sits right at the heart of the Christian life, one that most people never stop to examine. Drawing on two specific Greek words from the New Testament, he builds a case that will make you rethink how you approach prayer, faith, and the way you carry yourself in everyday life. There is a moment in this sermon involving a powerpoint and a wall socket that is surprisingly hard to shake, and a story about a battleship and a lighthouse that lands exactly where you would not expect it to.

Press play and find out why the thing you have been asking for might already be in your hands.

title: Money's Test
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
The way you spend money tells the truth about you, whether you are ready to hear it or not. Most of us know we probably should have a budget, but knowing and doing are very different things, and that gap might be costing you more than you realise.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge wraps up a four-week series on money with a straight-talking look at spending, the comparison trap, and why so many lottery winners end up worse off than before they struck it rich. He walks through six practical keys to spending wisely, drawing on some surprisingly direct wisdom from the Bible that has nothing to do with guilt and everything to do with freedom. Whether you feel anxious around money conversations or you have just never had anyone sit down and explain how all the pieces actually fit together, this one is worth your time.

Hit play and find out why the way you spend might be the real test of what you actually believe.

title: Money's Spirit and Surrender
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Ps Andrew Cartledge tells a story about a decision he and his wife made with their money that didn't work out the way he expected, at least not right away. What happened over the following year is the kind of thing that's hard to argue with once you've heard it.

In this episode, he walks through two principles most people never think about when it comes to their finances: seeding and saving. He challenges the idea that generosity is just about money, and takes the concept of sowing and reaping well beyond your bank account, into your workplace, your marriage, and even the way you think. This one will have you looking at your everyday decisions in a completely different way.

That story about the decision that didn't deliver the instant result he was hoping for, it turns out that's exactly the point.

title: Money's Pathway
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the way you handle money says more about what you actually believe than anything you'd ever say out loud? And what if the thing holding you back financially isn't your income, your circumstances, or your past, but something much closer to your own front door?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge walks through what the Bible actually says about money, and it might not be what you expect. He unpacks a concept called stewarding, and the way he frames it reframes the whole conversation around finances as something far bigger than budgets and bank balances. There are some honest questions here that are worth sitting with, and some old ideas about tithing and financial freedom that get a serious rethink. If you have ever felt like money has more control over your decisions than you would like to admit, this episode is going to give you something to chew on.

Hit play and find out what it actually looks like to stop serving money and start letting it serve you.

title: Money Misunderstandings
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Here is the podcast episode description:

Most of us will spend a third of our lives working to earn money, another third dreaming about having more of it, and the last third spending what we made. So why is it the one topic nobody wants to bring up in church?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church tackles the awkward silence head on. He walks through five common misunderstandings people hold about money, and some of them might surprise you, especially if you have assumed that financial freedom is something that only happens to other people. This is not a lecture about giving more or spending less. It is a honest look at where our ideas about money actually come from, and whether those ideas are working for us or quietly working against us.

Hit play and find out what the Bible actually has to say about money, and why it might be more relevant to your everyday life than you expected.

title: A Seat At The Table
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
What if you've spent years feeling like you missed the list, like everyone else got a seat but somehow yours was forgotten? And what if the very thing that made you feel disqualified is exactly what makes this story about you?

Ps Rachel Cartledge takes an unexpected detour through an ancient story most people have never heard of, and somehow it lands right in the middle of the everyday moments: dinner tables, lockdowns, broken promises, and the quiet ache of feeling like you are living in the middle of nowhere. There is a character in this episode who loses everything in a single day, ends up forgotten in a place whose name literally means "nothing," and who fully expects the worst when the king comes calling. What happens next is not what anyone in that room saw coming. This episode sits with the tension between what life promised and what it actually delivered, and it does not rush to a tidy answer.

Hit play and pull up a chair.

title: How To Have A Healthy Life Pt.3
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing holding you back from the life you actually want isn't your circumstances, your habits, or even your mindset, but something much deeper? And what if the weight you've been carrying around for years isn't something you can just think your way out of?

blurb:

title: Protection & Connection

blurb:

blurb:

blurb:

title: Peripheral Christianity

blurb:

Hit play and find out why the church might not be what you think it is, and why that matters more than ever.

title: He Tore Down The Walls

blurb:

Give it a listen when you get a chance.
